Louise Haigh, a former transport secretary who resigned due to a fraud conviction, has been appointed to the Cabinet Office by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, cementing her role as a central power broker.

The Bright Side:
Her experience in grassroots organizing and union work provides a rare, if currently misdirected, understanding of parliamentary staff conditions.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHO plane; the beneficiary is the Burnham-Haigh faction, not the public interest. It is a classic bait-and-switch: public service is the pretext for internal power consolidation.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic power-hoarding loop. By prioritizing personal loyalty over the ethical standards required for high office, the leadership creates a closed system that resists external scrutiny.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The alignment of factional interests creates a high-strain, unstable configuration.

The Unavoidable Truth: Political survival often relies on internal patronage networks rather than merit.

The Unavoidable Lie: This appointment is primarily about the public good and administrative efficiency.

This is a structural failure of accountability. By re-integrating a minister who resigned for fraud, the administration signals that factional utility outweighs the integrity of the office.
